issues.description: Email regex validation is basic and may not catch all invalid emails or allow some edge cases
issues.suggestion: Consider using a more robust email validation library like 'validator.js' or implement RFC 5322 compliant validatio);

issues.description: XSS sanitization is HTML-context specific and incomplete for all contexts
issues.suggestion: Consider using a dedicated sanitization library like 'DOMPurify' or 'sanitize-html' for comprehensive XSS prevention across different contexts (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, URL). For server-side, use context-aware encoding.

issues.description: ID generation using Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and may have collision risks at scale
issues.suggestion: Use a proper UUID library for guaranteed uniqueness: import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid'; return uuidv4(); or use crypto.randomUUID() in Node.js 16+

issues.description: Generic error messages don't provide enough context for debugging or user feedback
issues.suggestion: Use custom error classes with error codes: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(field: string) { super(`Validation failed for ${field}`); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } }

issues.description: Database interaction is commented out, making the code incomplete for production use
issues.suggestion: Either implement the actual database call or add a TODO comment explaining this is a mock/stub for testing purposes

issues.description: No maximum length validation on input fields could allow DoS via large payloads
issues.suggestion: Add length validation: if (input.name.length > 255 || input.email.length > 255) { throw new Error('Input exceeds maximum length'); }

issues.description: Missing error handling for database operations
issues.suggestion: Wrap database calls in try-catch: try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { throw new DatabaseError('Failed to save user', { cause: error }); }

issues.description: Email toLowerCase() is called without trimming whitespace first
issues.suggestion: Add trim() to handle whitespace: email: input.email.trim().toLowerCase(), This also improves data quality

codeQuality.summary: High-quality, secure code with proper input validation, XSS prevention, and SQL injection protection via parameterized queries. The code follows TypeScript best practices with clear interfaces, good documentation, and async/await patterns. Minor improvements suggested around validation robustness, ID generation security, and error handling specificity. No critical vulnerabilities detected.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is a security-critical function that determines whether user input is accepted. Incorrect validation could allow invalid emails or reject valid ones, impacting data integrity and user experience.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call isValidEmail('user@example') and expect it to return false (missing TLD). Call isValidEmail('user@example.com') and expect true. Call isValidEmail('user@@example.com') and expect false. Call isValidEmail('user name@example.com') and expect false (contains space). Call isValidEmail('') and expect false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The email regex may not catch all edge cases defined in RFC 5322. Testing edge cases ensures the validation logic handles unusual but valid/invalid email formats correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call isValidEmail('user+tag@example.com') and expect true (plus addressing). Call isValidEmail('user@sub.domain.example.com') and expect true (subdomain). Call isValidEmail('@example.com') and expect false (missing local part). Call isValidEmail('user@') and expect false (missing domain).

untestedPaths.reasoning: This function prevents XSS attacks by sanitizing user input. Any gaps in sanitization could lead to security vulnerabilities allowing script injection.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call sanitizeInput('<script>alert("XSS")</script>') and expect '<script>alert("XSS")</script>'. Call sanitizeInput("It's a test") and expect 'It's a test'. Call sanitizeInput('Normal text') and expect 'Normal text' (no changes).

untestedPaths.reasoning: The function should handle all XSS vectors and special character combinations. Missing edge cases could leave XSS vulnerabilities.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call sanitizeInput('') and expect '' (empty string). Call sanitizeInput('<>"\'\'"<>') and expect '<>"''"<>' (multiple special chars). Call sanitizeInput('Mix bold & "quoted"') and expect 'Mix <b>bold</b> & "quoted"'.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Creates users with validation and sanitization. This is a critical data handling function that combines multiple security checks. Failures could result in invalid user records or security breaches.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: 'John Doe'}) and expect a User object with sanitized name, lowercase email, generated id, and createdAt date. Mock saveUser to verify it's called with correct parameters.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Input validation prevents invalid data from entering the system. These are critical security and data integrity checks.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser({email: '', name: 'John'}) and expect it to throw Error('Email and name are required'). Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: ''}) and expect it to throw Error('Email and name are required'). Call createUser({email: 'invalid-email', name: 'John'}) and expect it to throw Error('Invalid email format').

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email case normalization prevents duplicate users with different case emails. Testing ensures emails are consistently stored in lowercase.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser({email: 'Test@EXAMPLE.COM', name: 'John'}) and expect the returned user.email to equal 'test@example.com'.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Name sanitization must prevent XSS when displaying user names. Failure to sanitize could allow stored XSS attacks.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: '<script>alert(1)</script>'}) and expect the returned user.name to equal '<script>alert(1)</script>'.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Generates unique user IDs. While uniqueness is important, the current implementation uses timestamp and random number which has low collision risk but should be tested for format consistency.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call generateId() twice and expect both results to start with 'user_'. Call generateId() twice and expect the two IDs to be different (uniqueness). Verify the ID format matches the pattern 'user_' followed by timestamp and random string.

untestedPaths.reasoning: ID collisions could cause data corruption. Testing uniqueness ensures the implementation generates distinct IDs.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call generateId() 100 times in a loop and collect results in a Set. Expect the Set size to equal 100 (all unique).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database interaction with parameterized queries. While the implementation is commented out, testing ensures proper query construction and parameter binding when implemented.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock the database query function. Call saveUser with a User object and verify the query string contains parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, $3, $4) and params array contains [user.id, user.email, user.name, user.createdAt] in correct order.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Async database operations could fail. Testing error handling ensures graceful failure when saveUser rejects.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock saveUser to throw an error. Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: 'John'}) and expect it to reject with the database error. Verify the error propagates correctly.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Ensures createdAt is set to a valid Date object at user creation time.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock Date.now() to return a fixed timestamp. Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: 'John'}) and expect user.createdAt to be an instance of Date. Verify the timestamp is close to the current time (within 1 second).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Functions should handle null or undefined inputs gracefully to prevent runtime errors.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call createUser({email: null, name: 'John'}) and expect it to throw Error('Email and name are required'). Call createUser({email: 'test@example.com', name: undefined}) and expect it to throw Error('Email and name are required').

suggestions.description: Replace multiple replace() calls with a single reduce or object-based mapping for better maintainability and performance
suggestions.benefits: Single regex pass instead of four, more maintainable escape map, easier to extend with new characters

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic into a separate validator using the Strategy pattern or dedicated validation service
suggestions.benefits: Separation of concerns (validation, creation, persistence), easier to unit test each component, follows Single Responsibility Principle, more extensible for additional validation rules

suggestions.description: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a dedicated library for more robust ID generation
suggestions.benefits: More secure random values, standard UUID format, eliminates collision risk from Date.now() timing, follows best practices for ID generation

suggestions.description: Implement Repository pattern to abstract database operations and make testing easier
suggestions.benefits: Repository pattern provides abstraction over data access, easier to mock for testing, supports dependency injection, allows switching database implementations without changing business logic

suggestions.description: Use const assertion or readonly for regex pattern to prevent accidental modification
suggestions.benefits: Regex compiled once at module load instead of every function call, clearer intent with uppercase naming, slightly better performance

suggestions.description: Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing for more concise validation
suggestions.benefits: More informative error messages, catches empty strings and whitespace-only strings, optional chaining prevents errors on undefined/null, better user experience

suggestions.description: Organize code using a service class to encapsulate user management logic with dependency injection
suggestions.benefits: Testable with dependency injection, encapsulates all user-related operations, maintains backward compatibility, supports multiple instances with different configurations, follows SOLID principles

refactorings.summary: The code is well-structured and follows security best practices, but there are several opportunities for improvement. Key recommendations: (1) Implement Repository pattern for better data access abstraction and testability, (2) Extract validation and factory logic into dedicated classes following Single Responsibility Principle, (3) Modernize ID generation using crypto.randomUUID(), (4) Optimize sanitizeInput with a single regex pass, (5) Improve error messages with more context, (6) Move to a service-based architecture with dependency injection for better testability and maintainability. Overall impact: HIGH - these refactorings would significantly improve code organization, testability, and maintainability while preserving all security features.

recommendations.description: Implement comprehensive test coverage for security-critical functions (isValidEmail, sanitizeInput, createUser). Currently at 0% coverage with 6 critical and 5 high-priority untested paths.
Implement Repository pattern to abstract database operations and improve testability. This will enable proper dependency injection and make the code more maintainable.
Replace Math.random() based ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() to eliminate collision risks and improve cryptographic security.
Enhance email validation using a robust library like validator.js for RFC 5322 compliance, and add input length validation to prevent DoS attacks via large payloads.
Extract validation logic into dedicated validator classes following Single Responsibility Principle. This improves testability and maintainability.
Optimize sanitizeInput function to use a single regex pass with an escape map instead of multiple replace() calls.
Implement custom error classes with specific error codes and context for better debugging and user feedback.
